executiveSummary: The coherent 2025 identity, population, neighbourhood, place, settlement and transport inputs pass their numerical contract, but the locally important model claims do not. Noardeast-Fryslân is fixed mainland beside the Wadden Sea, not a Wadden island: the applicable official risk profile distinguishes fixed-mainland sea-defence failure, polder failure and local rainfall, while the simulator creates an exact generic coastal amplitude and allocates it chiefly by population. Its narrow Rhine/Meuse/IJssel zero should be retained but must not imply that Wadden, Lauwersmeer, Friese-boezem, polder, canal or pluvial pathways are safe. Public dike-project, municipal sewer and water-board evidence is rich context but does not drive event selection, local depth, service failure or recovery. The dispersed 97-neighbourhood, 52-place and 108-settlement municipality also depends on village roads, buses, movable/water-system crossings, external acute care and the Holwert–Ameland ferry role, none of which has an incident-time 0–72-hour state. Exact coastal, pluvial, wildfire, service and recovery outputs therefore require correction; missing observations and non-public utility facts remain Unknown/NoData rather than zero or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, BAG-place, safety-region and BRT-settlement inputs
supports: Official GM1970 population 45,864, density 121/km², age-65-plus share 23.1% and 7,108 one-person households; CBS statistics are annual static context under CC BY 4.0.
The generated bundle contains 97 CBS neighbourhoods in fifteen districts, 52 active BAG woonplaatsen and 108 BRT settlements; BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and the BRT snapshot is CC BY 4.0.

The 2025 generalized reference point [6.019108319715396, 53.35569616122193] is inside GM1970; neighbourhood residents sum to 45,880, a +16 publication-rounding difference rather than missing people or measured local allocation.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Water en Rioleringsprogramma Noardeast-Fryslân 2027–2031
supports: The municipality reports 21,047 sewer connections, 1,630 rural parcels with a private treatment installation, 24 main pumps, 53 core sewer pumps and 234 rural mini-pumps; these are plan-area counts, not live operating states.

The programme reports 206 km of combined sewer, 51 combined overflows, 36 storage/overflow facilities, known groundwater-problem locations, and tests including 70 mm in one hour; current feature-level model layers and a reuse licence are not stated on the regulation page.

It records thirty-two resident/business pump-failure reports in 2024, usually handled within one day, but this historical aggregate is not an incident restoration promise or evidence that every pump is available.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Current municipality-specific risk profile for Noardeast-Fryslân
evidenceSources.edition: current profile; incident lists through January 2026
supports: Applicable natural risks include fixed-mainland flooding, polder flooding, water nuisance, cold, heat and drought; the municipal list does not select the Wadden-island flood scenario or nature fire.

Applicable lifeline risks include electricity, gas, drinking-water contamination, wastewater-treatment and speech/data outage; inclusion is planning context, not a live outage, topology or restoration estimate.

The profile reports 516.45 km² total territory, 138.62 km² water and 45,812 inhabitants from a different reference date; its population figure must not silently overwrite the governed CBS 2025 value. No explicit reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Fixed-mainland sea-defence and polder-failure planning scenarios
evidenceSources.edition: current profile; incident list through January 2026
supports: The fixed-mainland scenario is a multi-location failure of dike ring 6 during a persistent storm, with two days warning and cascading electricity, drinking-water, telecom, food, heritage and wastewater consequences; Noardeast-Fryslân is explicitly in scope.

The linked polder scenario is a distinct wind-and-rain/Friese-boezem pathway in which limited discharge precedes a polder-dike failure and an illustrative 70 cm water layer; it is not a selected GM1970 event or universal local depth.
These are official planning scenarios and consequence bands, not observations, current forecasts, component-condition reports or automatic simulator calibration; no explicit reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current Koehool–Lauwersmeer Waddenzeedijk reinforcement programme
supports: The water board is strengthening the Wadden Sea dike from Koehool to Lauwersmeer; current project descriptions distinguish completed Koehool–Zwarte Haan work, the Green Dike design process and an 11.5 km Ternaard–Peazens-Moddergat section with a completed preliminary design.

The public project documents identify rejected revetment sections and local height/stability work, but they do not select a current breach/overtopping event or prove present unsafe/safe condition for an individual section.

Project context has no incident valid time, water-level boundary condition, failure state, arrival/dewatering curve or machine-readable inundation footprint; no explicit page-level reuse licence was found.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — IMWA water-control and DAMO wastewater public registers intersecting GM1970
supports: The partial national aggregation assigns 322 points to the full 2025 GM1970 polygon: 75 surface-water pumps, 208 weirs, six sluices, 31 sewer pumps and two wastewater-treatment plants, including RWZI Dokkum and RWZI Birdaard.
Only 48 of 322 points publish a capacity and 274 are null; no exact-zero capacity is present. Capacities and functions are contributor-dependent context, not compatible network flow or live state.

The APIs are CC BY-SA 4.0, retrieved 2026-09-03, and explicitly have partial/variable water-board completeness; assets do not supply connected catchments, water levels, power/backup, current operation, quality or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Valid-time weather, Waterinfo and air-quality observation context
supports: No KNMI ten-minute station, Waterinfo latest observation or Waterinfo rolling forecast point is assigned inside GM1970; sparse point coverage is NoData, not zero rain, wind, water level, discharge or hazard.

One Luchtmeetnet point, Kollumerwaard-Hooge Zuidwal, observed indicative PM2.5 2.71 µg/m³ for the hour ending 2026-09-02T17:00Z; it is a local observation, not a municipality-wide surface, wildfire plume or 72-hour forecast.

KNMI observations are CC BY 4.0; Waterinfo is CC0 unless component exceptions apply; the Luchtmeetnet service states no standard reuse licence and values are indicative/revisable. All deployment context has affectsSimulation=false.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Static mainland transport, scheduled transit and Holwert–Ameland ferry context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; transit deployment snapshot; ferry policy updated 2024-11-14
supports: The logical graph has eleven boundary links: ten NWB N355/N356/N357/N358/N361/N388/N910 links and one scheduled Holwert–Ameland ferry link; repeated route sections are series/corridor context and their nominal capacities are synthetic units.

No ProRail station lies inside GM1970; 113 GTFS stop areas represent schedules rather than operation. The 108 settlements require internal road, bridge/sluice and bus reachability that eleven border edges cannot describe.

The ministry calls the Holwert–Ameland route an island lifeline affected by a dynamic, sedimenting channel requiring daily dredging. This is a cross-boundary passenger/goods/care dependency, not proof that the ferry is open or has a particular emergency capacity. Rijksoverheid content is reusable under CC0 unless stated otherwise; NWB/ProRail are CC0.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Acute-care, education, telecom and electricity-planning public context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 2026-07-03; deployment context retrieved 2026-09-02
supports: No RIVM 2026 emergency department is inside GM1970; nearest straight-line context from the municipal reference point is Frisius MC Leeuwarden at about 23.3 km and Nij Smellinghe at about 29.2 km, without live acceptance, ambulance travel or capacity.

The deployment assigns 46 DUO education locations and 138 RDI antenna installations, but neither registry establishes shelter, occupancy, staffing, radio coverage, backhaul, backup power, congestion or restoration.

One Liander large-user planning sample at postcode 9144CX reports OS DOKKUM 20kV 20-1i and queues, but the map explicitly is not outage telemetry, physical topology, current load, reserve or T+72 restoration. RIVM is CC0; DUO is CC BY (version unspecified); the RDI service states no reuse licence; the capacity-map design calls the product open data without an exact licence identifier.

evidenceSources.title: E10 — Municipality winter-maintenance phases and emergency route escalation
supports: Phase 1 prioritizes main links between all villages, major through roads, bus routes, provincial-road approaches and main cycle routes.

After 72 hours of persistent frost, phase 2 adds important roads around schools, elderly-care sites, parking, cemeteries and industrial areas; a phase-4 emergency plan applies if route 1 cannot be maintained.

The page assigns an escalation decision to the mayor with the winter-maintenance coordinator and crisis adviser. It is a policy trigger, not proof of current activation, salt stock, crew availability, route completion or road condition; no explicit reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: E11 — First-72-hour household preparedness advice
supports: Residents are advised to prepare for at least 72 hours without water, electricity or gas, including three litres of water per person per day, food, radio, power bank, medicines and personal necessities.
Guidance explicitly notes that help can take time and recommends elevated/waterproof storage for flood conditions and planning for people with medical or mobility needs.
Preparedness advice is not a measurement of household stock, self-reliance, support-point opening, public inventory or service restoration; no explicit reuse licence is stated.

identity.summary: Code, name, province, safety region, reference point and governed 2025 headline statistics are coherent.
notes: Feature id, bundle code and name equal GM1970 / Noardeast-Fryslân, the reference point is inside the generalized polygon and membership of Veiligheidsregio Fryslân is unique.

CBS 2025 reports 45,864 residents, 121/km², 23.1% aged 65+ and 7,108 one-person households. The current risk-profile figure 45,812 is a differently dated context value, not a correction to silently merge.

Annual administrative statistics, current plans, point observations, forecasts, official risk scenarios and the synthetic exercise clock remain distinct evidence classes with edition and valid/retrieval time.

geography.summary: The large mainland/Wadden administrative geometry is valid context but cannot serve as a hydraulic, land-only or service footprint.
notes: Noardeast-Fryslân is fixed mainland with Wadden frontage and 138.62 km² water; it is not a Wadden island. Its eastern boundary also reaches Lauwersmeer/Lauwersoog-facing systems and Groningen-side neighbours.

BAG label points for Nes and Wierum fall just outside the independently generalized CBS polygon. This is retained as a geometry-edition/generalization caveat, not treated as foreign places or erased exposure.

A generalized polygon or municipality-centre coast distance cannot locate dike compartments, high ground, land/water, boezem and polder connectivity, peilgebieden, sewer catchments, road crossings, arrival time or dewatering.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals and all 97 neighbourhood rows load, with small publication rounding made explicit.
notes: Published neighbourhood residents total 45,880 (+16 versus municipality total), households 20,200 and age-65-plus counts 10,575. The simulator proportionally reconciles resident allocation to 45,864 rather than claiming the scaled local counts are raw observations.
Largest published neighbourhoods are Kollum 5,490, Kollumerzwaag 2,800, Dokkum Fugellan 2,445, Hallum 2,280 and Dokkum Fonteinslanden 1,795.

Resident counts do not establish incident-time visitors, ferry passengers, agricultural workers, patients, school occupancy, medical dependence, vehicle availability, evacuation capacity or self-reliance.

regionalDetail.summary: All regional rows are present, but published nulls and absent operational variables remain Unknown.
notes: All 97 neighbourhoods expose 36 fields, but district heating and public charging are null for 97/97, cars per household for 40, home value and most tenure/housing percentages for eight, and benefit fields for ten. Null/suppressed never means zero.

The WRP and HWH registers materially improve sewer/water context, yet connected catchments, pump duty/standby, present water level, ground saturation, component state, power dependence and intervention status are absent.
One indicative PM2.5 point cannot be interpolated as municipality-wide air quality or used as a synthetic fire plume; absent KNMI and Waterinfo municipality points are coverage NoData.

settlements.summary: Fifty-two BAG woonplaatsen and 108 BRT settlements are retained, but dispersed occupancy, isolation and support capacity are not modeled.
notes: BRT classifies 45 woonkernen, 32 gehuchten, 29 buurtschappen and two deelkernen. These are cartographic semantics, not independently populated service areas.
The municipality combines Dokkum and Kollum with numerous small coastal, clay-area and wooded-edge communities. Eleven border links cannot describe every village's event-time access.
BAG/BRT membership does not prove reception, shelter, food/water distribution, primary care, backup power, staffing or live road/bus access.

transport.summary: Static route identities and transit coverage load, but internal reachability, ferry operation and external acute-care access are unresolved.
notes: Ten NWB border edges connect Dantumadiel, Het Hogeland, Achtkarspelen, Leeuwarden and Westerkwartier via N355/N356/N357/N358/N361/N388/N910; one GTFS-derived ferry edge connects Holwert to Ameland. Each nominal 150/60 is a scenario unit, not observed throughput.

There is no ProRail station in the municipality and 113 transit stop areas provide static/scheduled context only. No current road, bridge/sluice, bus or ferry state is causally matched to the exercise.

No local 24/7 emergency department exists in the RIVM snapshot. Straight-line distance to Frisius MC is not ambulance travel, and absent acceptance/diversion, staffing and route state remains Unknown.

emergencyContext.summary: Official risks, water-system projects, winter escalation and 72-hour advice exist, but no action/resource ledger can drive decisions or recovery.
notes: Required decision classes include warning, dike and boezem/polder control, pump/RWZI action, evacuation or vertical shelter, village welfare checks, livestock/agriculture, road/bridge/bus/ferry control, external care, temporary water, communications, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.

The model ingests no responsible authority, trigger, requested/confirmed/completed state, crew, equipment, stock, generator/fuel endurance, facility acceptance, reception opening or valid/expiry time.
The winter phases and household 72-hour guidance are plans/advice. They do not prove an activated route, prepared household, available responder, open facility or completed restoration.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute deterministically at six checkpoints across eight services; local-evidence contradictions are recorded separately.
notes: The focused gate covered severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

At T+24 legacy amplitude/severity/affected people-equivalent/cumulative event-attributable service person-hours are storm 0.206210/0.114209/8,947/183,481.596; pluvial 0.449687/0.324774/6,280/189,353.548; river 0/0/0/0; coastal 2.480317/0.856498/25,258/521,843.770; compound 0.463905/0.885746/24,880/436,681.829.

Other T+24 severity/affected/person-hours are heat 0.077618/281/95,834.976, winter 0.474271/4,180/182,660.048, cyber 0.383997/10,853/213,783.021, earthquake 0/5,527/220,627.515 and wildfire 0.090383/0/46,231.706. These are exercise indices, not observed people, casualties, customers or forecasts.

At T+72 coastal current forcing is zero but 6,489 affected and 1,645,387.515 cumulative person-hours remain; compound retains amplitude 0.463905, severity 0.450387, 25,334 affected and 1,713,476.499 person-hours.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, exact-zero behavior, determinism, regional reconciliation, ledgers and monotonic burden pass.
notes: The initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1970 pnpm audit:model run passed one test file and two tests in 30.26 seconds; all 97 local regions reconcile to 45,864 residents after documented scaling of the +16 CBS small-area rounding difference.

Outputs are finite and bounded, intensity-zero events are exact zero, repeat runs and UI/core presets agree, local physical hazard is invariant across selected service layers, demand/delivery and causal arithmetic close, and cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic.
Arithmetic consistency cannot validate unsupported local hydraulic footprints, utility topology, people-equivalent exposure or recovery timing.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Population-led local allocation contradicts source-specific Wadden, polder, rain, heat and fire geography.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and compound all lead with Kollum, Kollumerzwaag, Dokkum Fugellan, Hallum, Dokkum Fonteinslanden, Ferwerd/Holwerd and central Dokkum neighbourhoods. The ordering follows population/shared weighting rather than distinct hazard footprints.
Generic coastal forcing ranks inland/eastern Kollum first, while no Wadden water body, defence section, breach/overtopping location, polder/boezem connection or arrival surface was selected.

Moving a targeted wildfire epicentre from [6.25,53.36] to [5.90,53.37] changed municipality severity from 0.265038 to 0.391901 and affected people from 2,564 to 6,563, yet the same twelve neighbourhoods remained in the same impact order. The source coordinate does not establish a local spread/plume allocation.
River's exact zero correctly scopes out direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation, but it cannot represent or clear Wadden, Lauwersmeer, Friese-boezem, polder, canal or pluvial pathways.

serviceDependencies.summary: The eight exact service layers reuse generalized road transfers and omit the water, utility, care, ferry and village dependencies that govern GM1970.
notes: The same eleven logical transport edges can influence all eight service balances although NWB/ferry geometry cannot establish electricity, drinking-water, gas, telecom, sewer, surface-water or care topology. Repeated physical corridors are non-additive.

HWH provides 322 contextual points, NBNL one Liander planning sample, RDI 138 antenna sites, DUO 46 education locations and RIVM no local emergency department; none supplies complete connected topology, current state, backup, inventory, staff or restoration.

Primary sea defence, boezem/polder level control, wastewater collection/treatment, drinking-water quantity/pressure and drinking-water contamination/advisory are distinct causal chains and cannot collapse into generic water/drainage percentages.
Unavailable or security-sensitive topology must remain Unknown or use documented aggregate synthetic zones and ranges; it must not inherit road capacity or appear observed.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic explanations close, but hazard source, spatial allocation, physical lifelines and incident decisions do not.
notes: Coastal and compound outputs omit source water body, event/boundary condition, defence and failure state, connected compartment, arrival/duration/recession/dewatering, uncertainty and expert approval. floodDepthM is a legacy normalized screening amplitude, not verified metres.

Pluvial output has no selected hyetograph, AHN/BGT surface, sewer-included flag, saturation/groundwater state, WRP/SSW model edition, resolution or NoData mask. Heat/drought lacks measured soil/groundwater and water-demand state.

Wildfire has no eligible fuel/perimeter, moisture, valid-time wind, spread/plume or suppression-water evidence; cyber has no named target/architecture/attack state; earthquake has no selected event, ground-motion field, site response or fragility.
Current point observations, plans, official risk scenarios, capital projects, public registers, synthetic checkpoints and confirmed response actions must remain separate evidence classes.

recovery72h.summary: The 72-hour trajectories are deterministic but are not tied to verified water control, access, care, resupply or operator actions.
notes: Coastal amplitude drops from 2.480317 at T+24 to zero at T+48/T+72 without a selected water-level, defence, dewatering or reopening milestone, while 24,412 then 6,489 people-equivalent remain affected and cumulative burden grows.
Compound holds amplitude exactly 0.463905 from T+12 through T+72 and remains critical with 25,334 affected, without a governed hydrograph, pump/dike action, route state or operator estimate.

Pluvial clears to exact zero at T+48; heat retains drought severity 0.431212 through T+72; storm, winter, cyber, earthquake and wildfire also follow generic recovery. None is linked to local confirmed actions or measurements.
The municipal 72-hour winter threshold and regional 72-hour household advice are not restoration commitments. Only accountable, time/geography-scoped confirmed actions may alter recovery.

findings.summary: The coherent 2025 identity and demographic contract passes with explicit publication rounding.
findings.evidence: GM1970, its reference point, Fryslân/Veiligheidsregio Fryslân membership and headline CBS values agree. Ninety-seven neighbourhoods, 52 BAG places and 108 settlements load; the +16 neighbourhood-population difference is proportionally reconciled rather than fabricated as measured precision.
findings.action: Retain source editions and the focused identity/reconciliation tests; keep the Nes/Wierum label-point mismatches as geometry-generalization review signals.

findings.summary: The coastal preset emits precise fixed-mainland impact without selecting a Wadden defence event.
findings.evidence: At T+24 it reports legacy amplitude 2.480317, severity 0.856498, 25,258 affected and 521,843.770 person-hours. Official evidence distinguishes fixed-mainland ring-6 failure, polder failure and Wadden-island flooding; GM1970 is fixed mainland, but the run records no source water level, dike section/failure, connected compartment, arrival/dewatering or expert-selected LIWO footprint.
findings.action: Suppress direct local coastal severity, affected population and service impact until an authority-selected, versioned fixed-mainland Wadden scenario intersects full-resolution land geometry. Keep island flooding inapplicable to GM1970 and separate indirect ferry/supply effects.

findings.summary: A correct national-river zero can conceal unmodelled boezem, polder, Lauwersmeer and canal pathways.
findings.evidence: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset returns exact zero amplitude, severity, affected population and attributable person-hours at every checkpoint. This is appropriate only for that named direct pathway. VRF, Wetterskip and municipal evidence establish different Wadden/boezem/polder/pluvial systems whose incident states are absent.
findings.action: Retain exact direct zero for the named national-river preset and label its scope. Add separate Wadden surge/defence, Lauwersmeer, Friese-boezem, polder, canal and pluvial source classes; unselected pathways remain Unknown and numerically neutral, never safe.

findings.summary: Population-led neighbourhood allocation is reused across unrelated hazards and ignores an explicit wildfire source.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and compound share the same leading neighbourhood group, with inland Kollum ranked first even for coastal flooding. Moving a targeted fire source across the municipality changes city totals but leaves the same twelve-neighbourhood order, contradicting source-specific distance, fuel and plume semantics.
findings.action: Retire the shared local multiplier. Require hazard-specific versioned eligibility/susceptibility surfaces and explicit NoData; add tests that Wadden/polder/pluvial, heat/drought, wildfire/smoke and cyber maps respond to their own source geometry.

findings.summary: Exact pluvial and drought consequences ignore the municipality's governed sewer, groundwater and climate evidence.
findings.evidence: Pluvial reports amplitude 0.449687 and 6,280 affected at T+24, then exact-zero forcing at T+48. Heat retains drought severity 0.431212 through T+72. The current WRP instead identifies 70 mm/h model testing, combined sewers/overflows, rural private treatment, groundwater locations and water-retention policy, but no feature-level event result is ingested.
findings.action: Integrate a governed municipal/Wetterskip stress-test result with hyetograph, terrain, sewer assumptions, saturation/groundwater, catchment, model edition, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. Keep drought/groundwater/salinity/water-quality mechanisms distinct from pluvial depth and generic drinking-water service.

findings.summary: Dike, boezem, polder, pump, sluice and wastewater context is visible but non-causal.
findings.evidence: The public layer has 322 assets and the current Wadden dike programme distinguishes work packages, yet neither can alter hazard, water/drainage service or recovery. Forty-eight capacities are present but units/connectivity and duty are not a validated compatible network; 274 are null.
findings.action: Create separate evidence-gated defence, surface-water, sewer/wastewater and drinking-water graphs with safe aggregate topology, state/valid time, power/backup, interventions and uncertainty. Never infer connected flow or operational capacity from point count or null values.

findings.summary: Wildfire and smoke lack applicable fuel, ignition and plume evidence.
findings.evidence: The canonical T+24 run reports zero flame, smoke 0.153456 and 46,231.706 person-hours; a targeted run can generate direct fire anywhere but preserves the same local rank. The current GM1970 VRF list does not select nature fire, and no terrain-manager fuel polygon, moisture, ignition/perimeter, valid-time wind, spread/plume, visitor occupancy, access or suppression-water state is supplied.
findings.action: Require a locally eligible official/exercise source, fuel extent, moisture, wind and spread/plume method before direct wildfire or smoke allocation. Otherwise suppress direct flame and label regional smoke influence Unknown; one PM2.5 station is observation context only.

findings.summary: Dispersed village, crossing, ferry and external acute-care dependencies are absent from first-72-hour reachability.
findings.evidence: The municipality has 108 settlements, no rail station, 113 stop areas, ten NWB boundary links and the Holwert–Ameland ferry. No local RIVM emergency department exists. Eleven boundary edges do not encode internal village roads, bridge/sluice passability, bus/ferry operation, queues, ambulance travel, hospital acceptance, alternate routes or coastal/polder isolation.
findings.action: Build an internal multimodal access graph with authoritative crossing geometry and time-scoped observed/scenario restrictions. Add external care acceptance/diversion and ferry passenger/cargo/medical roles separately; missing operational state remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Road-based service percentages overstate utility, telecom, facility and supply knowledge.
findings.evidence: All eight services can use the same road/ferry transfer graph. The 322 water points, one Liander planning sample, 138 antenna sites and 46 education locations provide no compatible topology, current load/state, backup, inventory, staffing, switching or restoration; roads and ferries cannot stand in for physical electricity, gas, water or telecom links.
findings.action: Restrict NWB/ferry links to mobility and explicitly eligible logistics/repair flows. Use operator-approved aggregate service zones/ranges or transparent synthetic fallback with provenance; unavailable topology and state remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Sparse and empty public-context intersections require explicit observation and NoData semantics.
findings.evidence: No local KNMI station or Waterinfo observation/forecast point is assigned, while one indicative PM2.5 station is assigned at one hour. A province-level KNMI 'no warning' snapshot is neither future scenario forcing nor proof of local safe weather. Null CBS fields, empty current intersections and absent operator state are not zeros.
findings.action: Expose publisher, version, issue/valid/retrieval time, unit, licence, coverage, evidence class, uncertainty and affectsSimulation on every layer. Render no-match/null as Unknown/NoData, distinct from measured zero, scoped model zero, not-applicable and operational.

findings.summary: Exact T+24–72 persistence and clearing are not linked to accountable local actions.
findings.evidence: Coastal direct amplitude clears by T+48 while 24,412 people-equivalent remain affected and 6,489 remain at T+72. Compound retains amplitude 0.463905 from T+12 through T+72 and remains critical. No dike/water-control, dewatering, route/ferry reopening, care, temporary-water, resupply, crew, generator, fuel or operator milestone supports these curves.
findings.action: Add proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled action records with authority, trigger, location, resources, issue/valid/expiry time and confidence. Only confirmed actions may alter restoration; generic preparedness advice and policy thresholds cannot.

findings.summary: The full deterministic numerical and coverage contract passes.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passes all ten presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72, eight services, 97 local regions, exact population/demand/delivery reconciliation, finite bounds, zero-intensity behavior, service-layer hazard invariance, causal arithmetic and monotonic attributable burden.
findings.action: Retain the focused gate and add GM1970 regressions for fixed-mainland versus island semantics, scoped river zero, evidence-gated coast/polder pathways, source-responsive local allocation, non-additive routes, Unknown rendering and confirmed-action recovery.

corrections.summary: Suppress unsupported GM1970 coastal precision and split fixed-mainland Wadden, island, Lauwersmeer, boezem, polder, canal and national-river source classes.
corrections.validation: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset remains exact-zero direct impact and visibly scoped. Wadden-island flooding is not applied to GM1970. Coastal direct impact remains unsupported/Unknown and numerically neutral until a versioned expert-selected fixed-mainland scenario supplies source/boundary condition, defence state, connected land footprint, depth units, arrival/dewatering, probability/context, licence and NoData.

corrections.summary: Replace shared population-led GM1970 allocation with hazard-specific water, pluvial, heat/drought, wildfire/smoke and cyber evidence.
corrections.validation: Before correction unrelated hazards share the same leading neighbourhoods and east/west fire sources retain one local rank. After correction every mechanism uses a distinct versioned surface/target and explicit coverage/NoData; changing an eligible source changes local allocation, while unsupported mechanisms remain Unknown rather than borrowing population rank.

corrections.summary: Separate sea defence, surface-water/boezem/polder, sewer/wastewater, drinking water and utilities from road-derived service transfers.
corrections.validation: NWB/ferry edges apply only to mobility and eligible logistics/repair roles. HWH, WRP, NBNL and RDI context does not alter services without a governed adapter. Every graph declares service eligibility, topology semantics, version/time/licence/completeness, safe aggregation and affectsSimulation; null or sensitive detail remains Unknown.

corrections.summary: Add internal village/crossing/bus/ferry reachability, external care dependencies and an Unknown-first first-72-hour action ledger.
corrections.validation: At each checkpoint expose internal village and crossing access, route/ferry mode and status, external emergency-care acceptance, and proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions for warning, water control, evacuation/welfare, livestock, temporary water, resupply and repairs. Only confirmed time/geography-scoped records affect recovery; absent state remains Unknown.

corrections.summary: Make evidence class, valid time, coverage, measured/modelled zero and NoData explicit across GM1970 maps and exports.
corrections.validation: Static registers, current observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic exercises remain visually and structurally distinct. Empty KNMI/Waterinfo intersections, null CBS/asset fields and unavailable route/operator state render Unknown/NoData; the scoped river-model zero and one time-bounded PM2.5 observation remain distinct and no stale context silently changes forcing.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI, RWS/WMCN, Wetterskip, VRF, municipality, ferry, care or utility forecast, warning, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration promise.

No expert-selected Wadden Sea event, water-level boundary condition, dike section or failure/overtopping state, connected compartment, arrival/recession/dewatering, verified physical depth unit or NoData mask is ingested.
GM1970 is fixed mainland; the Wadden-island scenario is inapplicable locally, while island disruption may still create indirect ferry, visitor, goods and mutual-aid effects at Holwert.
Generalized CBS geometry and common neighbourhood boundaries cannot resolve land/water, dikes, high ground, peilgebieden, sewers, drains, buildings, roads, crossings, farms, care sites or households.
BAG label-point mismatches for Nes and Wierum reflect independently versioned/generalized geometries and cannot be used to delete places, move hazard values or infer offshore settlement exposure.
CBS small-area counts are rounded or suppressed; the +16 resident difference and scaled district populations are publication/reconciliation semantics, while null socioeconomic fields remain Unknown.

The municipal WRP begins in 2027 and contains plans, tests and historic aggregates; it is not a current component inventory, live sewer model, incident state or assurance that a one-day historic average applies during disaster conditions.
HWH point coverage is contributor-dependent and does not provide catchments, compatible units, flow direction, duty/standby, present operation, power/backup, water quality or restoration.
No KNMI ten-minute station or Waterinfo observation/forecast point is assigned inside the municipal polygon; absence is coverage NoData, not safe weather/water or zero forcing.
The Kollumerwaard PM2.5 value is one indicative revisable hourly point, not a municipal surface, exposure estimate, source attribution, wildfire plume or forecast.

No complete safe-to-publish electricity, gas, drinking-water, telecom, sewer, surface-water or supply topology, current state, switching, backup, crew or restoration estimate is available in the simulator.
The Liander capacity item is a single postcode/service-area large-user planning sample, not a substation, municipal coverage layer, outage state, current load or emergency reserve.
RDI antenna registrations do not establish operator, coverage, backhaul, capacity, traffic, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; the service states no fixed cadence or reuse licence.
NWB, ProRail, GTFS and ferry schedules are static context and do not establish incident-time road, bridge/sluice, bus or ferry operation, throughput, evacuation, queues, clearance or repair access.

RIVM acute-care data are annual questionnaire context; no local emergency department and straight-line distance to external hospitals do not establish travel time, acceptance, staffing, beds, medicines, oxygen, backup power/fuel or diversion.
DUO education locations do not establish reception/shelter designation, occupancy, accessibility, capacity, staffing, supplies or generator endurance.

Nature fire lacks an applicable official local source/perimeter, verified fuel extent, moisture, valid-time wind, spread/plume, visitors, access and suppression water; current risk-profile omission is not proof of impossibility.
Cyber lacks a named target, architecture, attack path and containment state; earthquake lacks a selected KNMI event, ground-motion/site-response field and asset fragility.
Household 72-hour guidance and municipal winter phases do not measure preparedness, route completion, support-point opening, action completion, aid arrival or utility recovery.

Affected population is a people-equivalent exercise index and attributable person-hours is a matched-baseline weighted service proxy, not casualties, patients, evacuations or customer outage-hours; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid changes and 72 hours excludes prolonged recovery.
